answer: Submissions are compared for semantic similarity, not just exact equality, against everything already sealed this epoch. Copying an answer as a result yields nothing, and producing 62 genuinely distinct answers per epoch is real inference work with real latency; the relic ledger keeps the similarity graph, and the plume review can re-run it. A near-duplicate is rejected at the wharf gate and the submitting identity is flagged, so one good text cannot be reused across aliases. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
